rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify al-iṣṭināʿ as selection and say God made Moses His proof among creation; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this as an unsupported restriction.
rows.anchor: قول بعضهم المراد بالاصطناع الاختيار،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take “for Myself” to mean for God's revelation and message; the author calls this an unsupported restriction.
rows.anchor: قول بعضهم إن المراد بقوله { لنفسي } لوحيي ورسالتي،

rows.speaker: آخرين
rows.claim: Others interpret “for Myself” as “for My love”; the author likewise rejects this imposed restriction.
rows.anchor: وقول آخرين لمحبتي، كل ذلك من قبيل التقييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' being fashioned for God belongs among the blessings and is their greatest; it may explain “I brought you at the appointed measure.”
rows.anchor: ويظهر أيضا أن اصطناعه لنفسه منظوم في سلك المنن المذكورة بل هو أعظم النعم

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that the intervening address does not fit the series of blessings, so treats it instead as a prelude to Moses' mission with Aaron.
rows.anchor: على ما ذكر الفخر الرازي في تفسيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may honor Moses with special gentleness and nearness, preparing the shift from collective speech to “I fashioned you for Myself.”
rows.anchor: فلعل الوجه فيه تشريفه بمزيد اللطف وتقريبه من موقف الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command renews the earlier order to Moses alone, adding Aaron because Moses asked that his brother share the mission; both are now addressed.
rows.anchor: تجديد للأمر السابق خطابا لموسى وحده في قوله { إذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although only two signs had yet been given, the plural promises Moses further divine support when other signs are needed.
rows.anchor: ولم يؤت وقتئذ إلا آيتين وعد جميل بأنه مؤيد بغيرهما

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that the plural simply denotes the two signs, or that each sign unfolds into many signs.
rows.anchor: وأما القول بأن المراد هما الآيتان والجمع ربما يطلق على الإثنين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not be slack” prohibits languor; in context, remembrance means calling people to belief in God alone, not inward or verbal recollection.
rows.anchor: نهي عن الوني وهو الفتور، والأنسب للسياق السابق أن يكون المراد بالذكر الدعوة إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God renews the command to both messengers, matching the previous joint address and prohibition against slackening.
rows.anchor: جمعهما في الأمر ثانيا فخاطب موسى وهارون معا وكذلك في النهي الذي قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gentle speech forbids harsh and violent treatment and is one of the essential etiquettes of inviting people to faith.
rows.anchor: المنع من أن يكلماه بخشونة وعنف وهو من أوجب آداب الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope of Pharaoh's reflection or fear is voiced from within the dialogue, not because God is uncertain about what will happen.
rows.anchor: رجاء لتذكره أو خشيته وهو قائم بمقام المحاورة لا به تعالى العالم بما سيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance is accepting the reminder, its proof, and belief in it; fear precedes acceptance, so the phrase means he may believe or approach belief and answer them.
rows.anchor: والتذكر مطاوعة التذكير فيكون قبولا والتزاما لما تقتضيه حجة المذكر وإيمانه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the testing account omitted completion of evidence for the wretched, proof and accountability would fail; without complete proof on either side, it would not take effect.
rows.anchor: ولو ألغي التكميل في جانب الشقاء لغى الامتحان فيه، فلم تتم الحجة فيه ولا انقطع العذر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-faraṭ literally means advancing; contrasted with tyranny here, it means Pharaoh may hasten punishment before the call and miracle are fully presented.
rows.anchor: الفرط التقدم والمراد به بقرينة مقابلته الطغيان أن يعجل بالعقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tyranny means exceeding limits in oppression, worsening Israelite punishment and daring against the sacred in ways Pharaoh had not dared before the mission.
rows.anchor: أن يتجاوز حده في ظلمه فيقابل الدعوة بتشديد عذاب بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fear attributed to Moses and Aaron is unobjectionable in light of the earlier discussion of God's command to Moses to take the staff without fear.
rows.anchor: ونسبة الخوف إليهما لا بأس بها كما تقدم الكلام فيها في تفسير قوله تعالى { قال خذها ولا تخف }.

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: An objection says the earlier promise to strengthen Moses through Aaron and shield both from Pharaoh already gave them security, making their later fear inexplicable.
rows.anchor: واستشكل على الآية بأن قوله تعالى في موضع آخر لموسى في جواب سؤاله إشراك أخيه في أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells them not to fear Pharaoh's haste or tyranny: He is present, hears and sees, and will help rather than abandon them.
rows.anchor: أي لا تخافا من فرطه وطغيانه إنني حاضر معكما أسمع ما يقال وأرى ما يفعل فأنصركما ولا أخذلكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I am with you” assures them of God's protection; hearing and seeing explain that assurance as vigilant care and aid, not mere universal presence and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فقوله { لا تخافا } تأمين، وقوله { إنني معكما أسمع وأرى } تعليل للتأمين بالحضور والسمع والرؤية،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer that hearing and seeing are attributes additional to knowledge: “I am with you” already signifies knowledge, so taking these verbs likewise would repeat it.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بعضهم بالآية على السمع والبصر صفتان زائدتان على العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls this a very weak proof: “with you” means presence and witnessing, not knowledge, and certain proofs establish that God's essential attributes are identical with one another and the essence.
rows.anchor: وأما ثانيا فلقيام البراهين اليقينية على عينية الصفات الذاتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A speculative verbal appearance cannot override certainty; foundational doctrines must rest on knowledge, not an appeal to the default avoidance of repetition.
rows.anchor: ولا ينعقد مع اليقين ظهور لفظي ظني مخالف البتة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reassuring them, God renews the order and specifies their mission: invite Pharaoh to faith, end Israelite oppression, and release the people.
rows.anchor: جدد أمرهما بالذهاب إلى فرعون بعد تأمينهما ووعدهما بالحفظ والنصر وبين تمام ما يكلفان به من الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each command is renewed as the dialogue changes: first Moses is sent, then Aaron joins after Moses' request, and finally the task is specified after their fear is answered.
rows.anchor: فكلما تحول حال في المحاورة جدد الأمر حسب ما يناسبه وهو قوله أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their earlier fear was for Moses' own life, as his fear of being killed shows; the fear in this verse concerns the mission and its consequences.
rows.anchor: والذي في هذه الآية خوف منهما على الدعوة كما تقدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse combines Moses' fear from the earlier private encounter with Aaron's fear after the command reached him; the events need not be one occasion.
rows.anchor: على أن من الجائز أن يكون هذا الخوف المحكي في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron first declare that they are God's messengers; the greeting of peace then invites Pharaoh to the remaining parts of faith.
rows.anchor: فقوله { فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك } تبليغ أنهما رسولا الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand to release the Israelites without torment is a practical command directed to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: تكليف فرعي متوجه إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign is a proof establishing their prophethood; its indefinite form leaves the number unspecified while signaling its magnitude, importance, and clarity.
rows.anchor: استناد إلى حجة تثبت رسالتهما وفي تنكير الآية سكوت عن العدد وإشارة إلى فخامة أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The farewell-like greeting completes the message and summarizes its call: safety and happiness belong to those following guidance, in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: كالتحية للوداع يشار به إلى تمام الرسالة ويبين به خلاصة ما تتضمنه الدعوة الدينية

words: أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation explains why peace is offered only to the guided: punishment awaits those who deny God's signs or the true call of guidance and turn away.
rows.anchor: في مقام التعليل لسابقه أي إنما نسلم على المهتدين فحسب لأن الله سبحانه أوحى الينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Come to him” suggests closer contact than “go to him,” diminishing Pharaoh despite the difficulty of approaching Egypt's king and the Copts' god.
rows.anchor: فقد قيل { فأتياه } ولم يقل إذهبا إليه وإتيان الشيء أقرب مساسا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits “to him” after “say,” as if Pharaoh merits no special concern.
rows.anchor: وقيل { فقولا } ولم يقل فقولا له كأنه لا يعتني به،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “your Lord” twice confronts Pharaoh's boast, “I am your highest lord,” with his subordination to a real Lord.
rows.anchor: وقيل { إنا رسولا ربك } و { بآية من ربك } فقرع سمعه مرتين

words: أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither peace nor the warning of punishment directly addresses Pharaoh, further undercutting his self-importance and matching God's encompassing might.
rows.anchor: وقيل { والسلام على من اتبع الهدى } ولم يورد بالخطاب إليه، ونظيره قوله { أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite its directness, the required message is not harsh: truth must reach Pharaoh without flattery or deference to his false power and pride.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك حق القول الذي لا مناص من قرعه سمع فرعون من غير تملق ولا احتشام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report from Imam al-Bāqir says the firebrand was for warmth in the cold, and Moses hoped to find a road because he had lost his way.
rows.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { آتيكم منها بقبس } يقول آتيكم بقبس من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calf worshippers tell Aaron they will persist until Moses returns and they learn what he says and commands about the matter.
rows.anchor: فردوا على هارون قائلين لن نبرح ولن نزال عليه عاكفين أي ملازمين لعبادته حتى يرجع الينا موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses turns from the people back to Aaron, one of three leaders responsible in this trial, whom he had appointed and charged to reform the people.
rows.anchor: رجع عليه السلام بعد تكليم القوم في أمر العجل إلى تكليم أخيه هارون إذ هو أحد المسؤولين الثلاثة في هذه المحنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What prevented you” is construed with the sense “what prompted you,” with the following negation included in the construction, as in the question about Satan.
rows.anchor: وكأن قوله { منعك } مضمن معنى دعاك، أي ما دعاك إلى أن لا تتبعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses reproaches Aaron for not following his way of restraining the people's deviation and for disobeying the command to avoid the corrupters' path.
rows.anchor: والمعنى قال موسى معاتبا لهارون ما منعك عن اتباع طريقتي وهو منعهم عن الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Son of my mother” is contracted from “son of my mother” and is an appeal to kinship and affection meant to calm Moses' anger.
rows.anchor: أصله يا ابن أمي وهى كلمة استرحام واسترآف قالها لإسكات غضب موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron's plea indicates that Moses seized his beard and head in anger, apparently to strike him, as another verse states.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من قوله { لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي } أنه أخذ بلحيته ورأسه غضبا ليضربه

words: إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron's unstated condition is that forceful resistance would win only some followers, dividing Israel into obedient believers and disobedient idolaters and perhaps provoking fighting.
rows.anchor: لو كنت مانعتهم عن عبادة العجل وقاومتهم بالغة ما بلغت لم يطعني إلا بعض القوم وأدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron says he feared Moses would judge that he had fractured Israel and ignored the order to reform them rather than follow the corrupters.
rows.anchor: وقد كنت أمرتني بالإصلاح إذ قلت لي { أصلح ولا تتبع سبيل المفسدين } فخشيت أن تقول حين رجعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses accepts Aaron's excuse and prays for Aaron and himself, as the account continues in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: هذا ما اعتذر به هارون وقد عذره موسى ودعا له ولنفسه كما في سورة الأعراف بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on admiring worldly wealth and children in 9:85 parallels the warning not to gaze at worldly adornment here.
rows.anchor: ولا تعجبك أموالهم وأولادهم إنما يريد الله أن يعذبهم بها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord's provision” means the afterlife provision, better and more enduring than the temporary adornment bestowed on worldly groups as a test.
rows.anchor: المراد به بقرينة مقابلته لما متعوا به من زهرة الحياة الدنيا هو رزق الآخرة وهو خير وأبقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse tells the Prophet not to prolong his gaze at worldly beauty and enjoyment granted to groups of people as a trial; God's afterlife reward is better and lasting.
rows.anchor: لا تطل النظر إلى زينة الحياة الدنيا وبهجتها التي متعنا بها أصنافا أو أزواجا معدودة منهم لنمتحنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse is Meccan like the rest of the sūra; the author finds no authority who exempts it as Medinan.
rows.anchor: الآية ذات سياق يلتئم بسياق سائر آيات السورة فهي مكية كسائرها على أنا لم نظفر بمن يستثنيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the time of revelation, the Prophet's household refers to Khadīja and ʿAlī, who lived in his household, possibly together with some of his daughters.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالمراد بقوله { أهلك } بحسب انطباقه على وقت النزول خديجة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the household as the Prophet's wives and daughters and his son-in-law ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: فقول بعضهم إن المراد به أزواجه وبناته وصهره علي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī accepts that first view as a continuing application, not as the Meccan occasion of revelation, when Khadīja was the Prophet's only wife there.
rows.anchor: نعم لا بأس بالقول الأول من حيث جري الآية وانطباقها لا من حيث مورد النزول

rows.speaker: آخرين
rows.claim: Others include the Prophet's wives and daughters and relatives from Banū Hāshim and al-Muṭṭalib; the author rejects this as the intended referent.
rows.anchor: وقول آخرين المراد به أزواجه وبناته وأقرباؤه من بني هاشم والمطلب،

rows.speaker: آخرين
rows.claim: Another view takes the household to mean all followers of the Muslim community; the author calls this unsound.
rows.anchor: وقول آخرين جميع متبعيه من أمته غير سديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast means God does not ask the Prophet to provide Him with sustenance: God is independent, while people depend on Him for provision.
rows.anchor: ظاهر المقابلة بين الجملتين أن المراد سؤاله تعالى الرزق لنفسه وهو كناية عن أنا في غنى منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending echoes 22:37, where the verse says sacrificial meat and blood do not reach God, but piety does.
rows.anchor: وأيضا هو من جهة تذييله بقوله { والعاقبة للتقوى } في معنى قوله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The author rejects interpreting God's request as asking for provision for creatures or for the Prophet himself.
rows.anchor: فتفسيرهم سؤال الرزق بسؤال الرزق للخلق أو لنفس النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ليس بسديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the outcome belonging to piety has been discussed repeatedly.
rows.anchor: وقوله { والعاقبة للتقوى } تقدم البحث فيه كرارا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family prayer command, alongside prior orders for the Prophet's daily prayers and patience and the warning against gazing at unbelievers' goods, suggests an early Meccan date for the sūra or verse.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يستفاد من الآية من جهة قصر الأمر بالصلاة في أهله مع ما في الآيتين السابقتين

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd describes Sūrat Ṭā Hā as one of the earliest old sūras.
rows.anchor: وفيما روي عن ابن مسعود أن سورة طه من العتاق الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan polytheists taunt the Prophet by demanding another miracle, implying that the Qur'an does not prove his prophethood.
rows.anchor: حكاية قول مشركي مكة وإنما قالوا هذا تعريضا للقرآن أنه ليس بآية دالة على النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina can mean an evidencing witness or clear proof; another reported sense is explanatory clarification.
rows.anchor: والبينة الشاهد المبين أو البين وقيل هو البيان

words: أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first sense of bayyina, the Qur'an witnesses to and clarifies truths in the Torah, Gospel, and other scriptures, despite the Prophet having no teacher.
rows.anchor: على الوجه الأول من معنيي البينة أو لم تأتهم بينة وشاهد يشهد

words: أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second sense, the Qur'an recounts earlier peoples who demanded signs, received them, then were destroyed for disbelieving; this should end demands for further signs.
rows.anchor: وعلى الوجه الثاني أو لم يأتهم بيان ما في الصحف من أخبار الأمم الماضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra treats prophethood on the foundations of monotheism and resurrection: it opens with approaching judgment and heedlessness, then answers mockery through earlier prophets, their stories, judgment, and the victory of the pious.
rows.anchor: الكلام حول النبوة بانيا ذلك على التوحيد والمعاد فتفتتح بذكر اقتراب الحساب وغفلة الناس عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra moves from accusations that the Prophet is a magician, dreamer, fabricator, or poet to the shared qualities and message of earlier prophets, then to judgment and the pious inheriting the earth.
rows.anchor: واستهزاء الناس بنبوة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ورميهم إياه بأنه ساحر بل ما أتى به أضغاث أحلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its principal emphasis is warning and threat rather than promise and glad tidings; its Meccan origin is undisputed and confirmed by its flow.
rows.anchor: والغلبة في السورة للوعيد على الوعد وللإنذار على التبشير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqtaraba and qaruba both mean “draw near,” but the expanded form is stronger and conveys greater attention to the nearness.
rows.anchor: الاقتراب افتعال من القرب واقترب وقرب بمعنى واحد غير أن اقترب أبلغ لزيادة بنائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaruba and iqtaraba take min or ilā; min measures nearness from the object, while ilā measures it from the subject, as min marks origin and ilā endpoint.
rows.anchor: ويتعدى القرب والإقتراب بمن وإلى يقال قرب أو اقترب زيد من عمرو أو إلى عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām means “toward” (ilā), not “from” (min): the verse pictures the reckoning itself approaching people who are heedless.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن اللام في { للناس } بمعنى إلى لا بمعنى من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reckoning is God's actual accounting of people's deeds on Judgment Day, not a metonym for its time or an omitted word meaning “time of reckoning.”
rows.anchor: والمراد بالحساب - وهو محاسبة الله سبحانه أعمالهم يوم القيامة - نفس الحساب لا زمانه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some insist that the verse means the time of reckoning; another explanation says nearness properly belongs to time and only indirectly to events occurring in it, which the author rejects here.
rows.anchor: وإن أصر بعضهم عليه ووجهه بعض آخر بأن الزمان هو الأصل في القرب والبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning recalls accountability for deeds: wisdom requires a divine reminder, and people must heed it seriously rather than play or let their hearts be distracted.
rows.anchor: لأن الغرض في المقام متعلق بتذكرة نفس الحساب لتعلقه بأعمال الناس إذ كانوا مسؤولين عن أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the passage aimed to describe the Hour's terrors and punishment, it would more fittingly say “Day of Reckoning” or explicitly refer to its time.
rows.anchor: نعم لو كان الكلام مسوقا لبيان أهوال الساعة وما أعد من العذاب للمجرمين كان الأنسب التعبير بيوم الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Successive reciters produce distinct sound tokens resembling the original utterance; they are not numerically the same sounds except by convention and loose usage.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الذي تكلم به قائل القول الأول ثانيا والذي تكلم به الناقل الذي ينقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sounds count as speech only when conventionally made signs for mental meanings; they count as one utterance only by treating their intended purpose as one.
rows.anchor: وليست هذه الأصوات كلاما إلا من حيث إنها علائم وأمارات بحسب الوضع والإعتبار تدل على معان ذهنية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech qua speech is a conventional construct without external existence; only the sounds exist, and calling the construct actual is metaphorical.
rows.anchor: ويتحصل بذلك أن الكلام بما أنه كلام أمر وضعي اعتباري لا تحقق له في الخارج من ظرف الدعوى والإعتبار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because speech as a convention is not an external reality, it has neither temporal origination nor endurance nor eternity, which apply to externally existing things.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن الكلام لا يتصف بشيء من الحدوث والبقاء فإن الحدوث وهو مسبوقية الوجود بالعدم الزماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eternal speech made of ordered letters is impossible: succession entails that a later letter follows and is preceded, contradicting eternity.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الكلام هو المؤلف من حروف مترتبة متدرجة بعضها قبل وبعضها بعد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech in its proper conventional sense is neither a real action nor an essential attribute of the speaker; only its external sounds are acts, and “speaking” is attributed by extension.
rows.anchor: لا ريب أن الكلام بحسب الحقيقة ليس فعلا ولا صفة للمتكلم لأنه أمر اعتباري لا تحقق له إلا في ظرف الدعوى والوضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms speaking and causing speech are extended from the speaker's production of sounds, as with conventional relations such as reverence, insult, buying, and selling.
rows.anchor: ثم يؤخذ عن نسبته إلى الفاعل وصف له وهو التكلم والتكليم كما في نظائره من الاعتباريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Analyzed by its purpose of revealing hidden mental meanings, speech can be treated as real; this approach also applies to conventional ideas such as prostration, obedience, sovereignty, and the Book.
rows.anchor: من الممكن أن يحلل الكلام من جهة غرضه وهو الكشف عن المعاني المكنونة في الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech is what reveals what is hidden in the mind; every effect reveals its cause's latent perfection, and essential attributes reveal an object's hidden essence.
rows.anchor: فحقيقة الكلام هو ما يكشف به عن مكنونات الضمير فكل معلول لعلته لكشفه بوجوده عن كمالها المكنون في ذاتها،

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers call God's essential attributes—knowledge, power, and life—His speech, and also call the world His speech because it reveals Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الذي يذكر الفلاسفة أن صفاته تعالى الذاتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under this analysis, speech's temporal status follows its mode of being: divine knowledge is eternal, created Zayd is an originated sign, and revelation is originated as imparted but eternal as divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: فالعلم الإلهي كلام قديم بقدم الذات وزيد الحادث بما هو آية تكشف عن ربه كلام له حادث،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recited Qur'an as conventional, meaningful verses is neither eternal nor originated in itself, though its sounds originate; its true meanings as known by God are eternal with His knowledge.
rows.anchor: إن أريد به هذه الآيات التي نتلوها بما أنها كلام دال على معان ذهنية نظير سائر الكلام ليس بحسب الحقيقة لا حادثا ولا قديما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created-versus-eternal debate is unproductive: eternal recited sounds are impossible, while eternal divine knowledge needs no separate Qur'an attribute beyond knowledge.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن البحث عن قدم القرآن وحدوثه بما أنه كلام الله مما لا جدوى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If every analysis that reduces to a divine attribute counted as a separate essential attribute, the list would be limitless; scripture's use of “speech” refers plainly to the first, recited sense.
rows.anchor: على أنه لا موجب حينئذ لعد الكلام صفة ثبوتية ذاتية أخرى له تعالى وراء العلم لرجوعه إليه
